business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law system with Common Law-inspired adaptations in commercial, maritime, and corporate legislation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force since 31 October 2012)
European Union–Central America Association Agreement (Panama as Contracting Party)
Panama–Republic of Korea Trade Promotion Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley No. 12 de 14 de marzo de 2017; Ley No. 41 de 2 de julio de 2000 (AML regime) as comprehensively amended by Ley No. 23 de 30 de octubre de 2015; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 54 de 1 de julio de 2011; Ley No. 52 de 27 de octubre de 2016 and its regulations establishing the mandatory Beneficiary Registry (Registro de Beneficiario Final) of legal entities; FATF mutual evaluation obligations and the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) guidance on beneficial ownership and PEP screening.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Founding Charter (Acta Constitutiva) and Foundation Bylaws (Reglamento)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría del Circuito) and Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only for bilingual/foreign signatures; registry original or certified copy filed domestically

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Founder's and Beneficiary's National Passport (biographical page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the founder's/beneficiary's state of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing state; if non-Hague member, consular legalization at the competent Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Proof of Residential or Business Address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or licensed financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing of a corporate founder (if any) and signed UBO chain declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or statutory corporate agent of the founder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the incorporating state; otherwise consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of the foundation founder, council members, protector, registered agent, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury UK Sanctions List, and the national Panamanian designations published by the UAF. PEP persons (heads of state, senior ministers, military flag officers, central bank boards, and their family members) trigger enhanced due diligence including source-of-funds verification via a licensed Panamanian ABA bank or a monitored aviation escrow account, corroboration of funds against the ISIC 4659 aviation spares sales pipeline, and mandatory Suspicious Transaction Report filing to the UAF under Ley 23 de 2015 whenever the PEP link is unexplained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – exclusive name clearance through the licensed agent via the 'Sistema de Ventanilla Electrónica' (electronic window) of the Public Registry of Panama (registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be in Spanish or any Latin-alphabet language; non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK ideographs) must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters and may be accompanied by a Spanish translational variant; the foundation standard prefix is 'Fundación de Interés Privado' but corporate-style names ending in 'S.A.', 'Inc.', 'Foundation', or descriptive trading suffixes are accepted; names must be distinct from existing registry entries and standard established nomenclatural rules prohibit confusing similarity with registered societies, foundations, or trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bank, Trust, Financiera (requires prior SBP financial license clearance)
Seguros, Reaseguros, Insurance (requires Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá authorization)
Fondo de Inversión, Fondos, Mutual Fund (requires Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores clearance)
Gobierno, Nacional, Estado, República de Panamá, Ministerio (state-patronage terms requiring prior ministerial approval)
Aviación, Aerolínea, Aeropuerto, Aeronáutica (special prior review by the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil for aviation-sector trading names)
Universidad, Colegio, Escuela (educational authority prior approval)
Mafia, Cartel, Terrorismo, Nazi (terms contrary to public order and Panamanian criminal policy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registry's Mercantile Section, the registered agent must (i) obtain the written denial notice and, within the same 30-day window, submit an alternative name for availability; (ii) if the denial rests on confusing similarity, file a formal 'Solicitud de Reconsideración' addressed to the Dirección General del Registro Público within 5 business days of notification, attaching a comparative schedule distinguishing the proposed name from prior registrations; (iii) if the denial rests on a sensitive token, secure the applicable 'Autorización Previa' from the sector regulator (e.g., the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil for aviation-related names); and (iv) if administrative reconsideration fails, commence a 'Recurso de Apelación' before the Jerarca of the Registry, and subsequently a 'Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa' before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia for infringement of the right of establishment under Ley 25 de 1995.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office registered at the licensed resident agent's address is acceptable for the Public Registry and UBO compliance; however, for the ISIC 4659 (aviation rotables and avionics surplus) activity, the Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil and the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias may require a demonstrable physical place of operations for the spares distribution license, and Panamanian banks exercising SBP KYC rules will independently demand commercial substance evidence (lease agreement, inventory records, aviation escrow arrangements) before onboarding the foundation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate aggregated risk: estimated under 5% for purely passive registry file-keeping, rising to approximately 10–15% during the first 24 months where the foundation maintains a Panamanian bank account and applies for the aviation spares supplier authorization, with a stated likelihood of unannounced UAF/Registry or SBP on-site verification at the licensed agent's office; maintaining a dedicated sub-lease desk and aircraft parts inventory registration at the agent's facility materially lowers the inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name availability certificate (Certificado de Disponibilidad de Nombre) - Public Registry of Panama
Registration fee for the Foundation Founding Charter (Derechos de Registro del Acta Constitutiva) - Public Registry of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on capital schedule

Initial UBO declaration filing (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) with the Beneficiary Registry platform
Registered agent and statutory office services - first year (resident licensed agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for PIF annuity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign passport, address proof, and corporate incumbency certificates (3 documents at 90 USD each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the document's state of origin and Panamanian Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-document tariff and consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn Spanish translation and notarization of foreign documentary evidence
AML/CFT pre-incorporation KYC package - PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and domestic sanctions screening and UBO chain verification for founder, council, protector and beneficiaries
Professional legal fees for structuring, charter drafting, registry follow-up and counsel opinions for the aviation spares trading scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, particularly Articles 6 (creation), 8 (governing instrument), 16 (initial endowment assets), 20-21 (registration and legal personality), 27-30 (foundation council governance and tax exemption), and 33-36 (dissolution); supplemented by the Public Registry Regulations and AML Law N° 23 of 27 April 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Fundacional (Foundation Charter / Escritura Pública de Constitución) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995, Article 16 requires an initial endowment of at least US$10,000.00. The endowment must be declared in the Foundation Charter and certified by the Founder. Full cash deposit is not mandatory at registry stage; however, for AML compliance under Law 23 of 2015 and for opening a Panamanian corporate bank account, the endowment is typically transferred through a licensed Panamanian bank into an escrow or registered-agent trust account, evidenced by a notarized contribution statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Founder hereby subscribes and declares the initial endowment of US$10,000.00 pursuant to Article 16 of Law 25 of 1995, and the Foundation acknowledges receipt of said endowment. (2) The registered office of the Foundation shall be established at [Registered Agent Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the registered agent is ratified. (3) The following individuals are appointed to the Foundation Council: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each serving until resignation or removal. (4) The Foundation Council is authorized to open bank accounts, execute aviation-parts supply contracts, and engage in the distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus. (5) All officers and the registered agent are authorized to tender the Foundation Charter for inscription at the Public Registry of Panama.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicio de Búsqueda de Nombres (Public Registry Name Search Desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written Spanish-language application listing up to three proposed foundation names (e.g., 'ATLANTIC AERO SPARES FOUNDATION'), together with the applicant's identification and proof of payment of the B/.5.00 search fee. The Registry will issue a Certificado de Búsqueda evidencing that the selected name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity.
required_dossiers: Written name-search application in Spanish
Copy of applicant's passport or Panamanian cédula
List of three alternative foundation names in priority order
Proof of payment of the name-search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is deemed identical or confusingly similar, file a second application with alternative names; the Registry reserves an available name for 30 days pending submission of the Foundation Charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Panama City Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct licensed Panamanian counsel to prepare the Spanish-language Acta Fundacional containing: (1) foundation name; (2) registered office; (3) initial endowment of US$10,000.00; (4) object clause covering the acquisition, marketing, and distribution of certified surplus civil aircraft rotables and avionics; (5) Foundation Council members and any Protector; (6) beneficiary and succession rules; and (7) AML declarations. Execute the deed before the notary by the Founder or the Founder's attorney-in-fact.
required_dossiers: Drafted Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional)
Passport copies of Founder, Foundation Council members, and Protector (if any)
Notarized and apostilled/consularized power of attorney issued to the Panamanian attorney (if Founder is absent)
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
Proof of registered-agent address and law-firm license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to incomplete KYC or identification documents, supplement the file with bank reference letters or certified translations and re-execute the deed within 30 days without additional statutory penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarial testimonio (certified copy) of the Acta Fundacional together with the completed application form and proof of payment of the registry tariffs (B/.60.00 for the first folio plus B/.15.00 per additional folio, plus stamp and certification fees, aggregating approximately US$250–450). Request issuance of the Ficha de Persona Jurídica and the certificate of inscription attesting the Foundation's legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarial testimonio of the Foundation Charter
Public Registry application form signed by the registered agent
Proof of payment of Public Registry tariffs
Power of attorney from the Founder to the registered agent
Identification copies of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a nota de impedimento, the attorney files a corrective submission (escrito de subsanación) within 10 business days; contested determinations may be appealed to the Registry's legal counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Ventanilla Única de Registro RUC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following inscription, apply online through the DGI e-Tax portal for the Foundation's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes). Submit the certificate of inscription, the inscribed Foundation Charter, and Foundation Council minutes designating the tax representative and fiscal domicile. The Foundation is registered under Panama's territorial income-tax regime, under which only Panama-source income is taxable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Signed RUC application form (solicitud de inscripción)
Foundation Council minutes designating the tax representative
Copy of registered agent's law license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is rejected for address or powers discrepancies, file a notarial certificate correcting the registry data and resubmit the application within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operation Notice and Zoning Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales / Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for commercial warehousing and trading of aircraft parts, attaching the RUC certificate, inscription certificate, lease contract, and the municipal zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo). Pay the municipal patent fee based on declared capital and obtain the municipal operation license; renew annually according to the municipality's fiscal calendar.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación application form
Foundation RUC certificate
Certificate of inscription of the Foundation
Lease agreement for registered premises and warehouse
Municipal zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo)
Proof of payment of municipal patent fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning certificate shows non-conforming warehouse use, request a special-use exception from the Dirección de Obras y Construcciones, or relocate to an approved commercial/industrial zoned premises and re-file the Aviso de Operación.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Aviation Authority Registration and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil (AAC) – Dirección de Seguridad Aérea; and Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for registration as an Aircraft Parts Distributor with the AAC by submitting the corporate docket, a quality and traceability manual aligned with FAA Advisory Circular AC 00-56A, inventory segregation procedures for serviceable versus unserviceable rotables, and certification documentation. In parallel, schedule an on-site fire-safety inspection by the Bomberos, install required extinguishers, emergency egress, and signage, and obtain the Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios for the warehouse.
required_dossiers: AAC application form for aircraft parts supplier registration
Certificate of inscription and RUC certificate
Municipal Aviso de Operación certificate
Quality and traceability manual (AC 00-56A aligned)
Inventory tagging and segregation procedures for certified rotables and avionics
Fire-safety inspection report and Bomberos fee receipt
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for hazardous components (batteries, compressed gases) in inventory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AAC requests supplemental information, respond within 10 business days with a complete expediente; if the Bomberos inspection fails, correct the deficiencies and request re-inspection within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Aeronáutica Civil (AAC) de Panamá – Dirección de Seguridad Aérea (Civil Aviation Authority, Directorate of Flight Safety); supplementary import/customs registration with the Dirección General de Aduanas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Registro del Distribuidor de Partes Aeronáuticas (Aircraft Parts Distributor Registration Certificate) and Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Operation Notice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (Registro de Impacto Ambiental) for warehouse and trading operations without industrial transformation; a full environmental impact study (Categoría II/III) is required only if aircraft-part painting, chemical stripping, plating, or engine overhaul operations are added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the public sewer must comply with DGNTI-COPANIT 35-2000 (pH 6–9; BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L; TSS ≤ 220 mg/L; oil and grease ≤ 20 mg/L). Solvents and degreasers must be stored in sealed containers with secondary containment; air emissions from solvent handling must be controlled by capture/extraction ventilation. Spent oils, batteries, and chemical waste are classified as special management waste under Law 18 of 2016 and must be transported by MiAMBIENTE-authorized hazardous waste haulers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certification of the warehouse, including extinguishers, emergency exits, and signage; structural and electrical load inspection certified by a Panamanian licensed engineer for racking and storage heights; occupational health and safety clearance by MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral), including a workplace hazard register, PPE program, accident reporting, and worker training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); taxpayer portal: SIT (Sistema Integrado de Tributación) at https://sit.mef.gob.pa/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in taxable economic activities in Panama must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from the DGI. For a PIF, the foundation's constitutive documents must be legalized and, where appropriate, apostilled, together with the Public Registry of Panama founding inscription and a notarized power of attorney appointing a local resident agent and fiscal representative. The application must be filed through the DGI's SIT portal or at a local DGI branch, specifying the foundation's name, registered address, and intended activities. If no Panamanian-source income is derived and no ITBMS registration is required, the PIF may remain tax-unregistered for income tax purposes, but any import, export, or local commercial transaction in Panama will require an RUC and corresponding registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no U.S.-style 'check-the-box' classification election. A Private Interest Foundation is a juridical person with autonomous patrimony; for Panamanian income tax purposes, Panamanian-source income is taxable at the entity level, while foreign-source income falls outside the territorial scope. No hybrid mismatch election or pass-through classification is available under the current Code; however, a qualifying small taxpayer may elect the simplified ITBMS regime if annual taxable turnover is below the relevant statutory threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panamanian Value Added Tax on transfers of movable goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 150,000 (Balboas per year) for the simplified small taxpayer regime; ITBMS registration is otherwise mandatory upon any habitual taxable transfer or import into Panama, and no general monetary threshold applies to commercial operators.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama does not currently operate a mandatory continuous transaction control clearance system, but the DGI requires electronic fiscal invoicing (factura electrónica) for most operationally active taxpayers, phased in by taxpayer category through the SIT portal. Invoices must include a DGI-issued digital fiscal code or authorized printed fiscal code where applicable, and transaction data, including export e-invoices, must be transmitted to the DGI on prescribed reporting cycles. Taxpayers must use DGI-authorized electronic invoicing software or the SIT web tool; real-time transactional interface is required for certain high-risk and large-taxpayer categories, while smaller taxpayers may issue electronic invoices with batch submission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports from Panama of tangible movable goods, including surplus commercial civil aircraft rotables and avionics parts, qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when the goods are physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination and the seller retains proof of export. Offshore services rendered to non-residents for use entirely outside Panama, and goods supplied into a Panamanian foreign trade zone for subsequent export, are also eligible. The exporter must be the registered seller, hold a valid RUC, and must not have consumed the goods within Panama before shipment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panama.
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT/FX credit evidence confirming payment of the export proceeds into the seller's Panama bank account.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and Customs Authority can retroactively reverse zero-rated treatment and claw back uncollected ITBMS, VAT credits, and refunds if the export documentation is inconsistent or non-existent. Penalties include fines ranging from 100% to 300% of the tax evaded, surcharges and default interest, suspension or cancellation of the RUC and customs registry license, and criminal tax fraud charges under Panama's Fiscal Code and anti-money-laundering laws. Directors, resident agents, and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for fraudulent export schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) in coordination with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama); the Republic of Panama does not maintain a conventional central bank issuing domestic currency, and the U.S. dollar serves as legal tender under Decree Law No. 9 of 1970. Currency control and anti-money laundering oversight are also exercised by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa exists purely as a unit of account and circulates only as coins pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar; the economy is fully dollarized with no separate legal tender. Accordingly, there is no discrete convertibility control over the U.S. dollar, and current-account payments for trade in goods and services are unrestricted. Capital account flows, including inbound equity or shareholder loans to a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), likewise do not require prior central bank approval because no foreign exchange surrender or licensing regime applies. However, for a PIF engaged in the distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, the practical profit-remittance constraints are not exchange-control related but arise from economic substance expectations, beneficial ownership documentation, and U.S. dollar clearing correspondent bank due-diligence requirements in jurisdictions where the ultimate beneficial owner or counterparties are located. Dividends or distributions to non-resident beneficiaries are not subject to Panamanian withholding tax under the territorial tax regime, provided the income derives from foreign sources or export-related activities, but banks will require full corporate and foundation documentation to distinguish the foundation's own assets from beneficiary interests for anti-money laundering and FATCA/CRS purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds or to convert foreign currency receipts into local currency, as the U.S. dollar is legal tender and the balboa has no independent exchange rate. Exporters of aviation parts and rotables may retain all proceeds in U.S. dollar-denominated accounts at licensed banks or at specialized escrow institutions. The relevant compliance obligations are documentary: export declarations must be filed with the Dirección General de Aduanas (Customs Authority) via the SISCOMEX-type platform for the verification of the Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación), and banking records must evidence an underlying commercial contract, commercial invoice, airway bill, certificate of airworthiness, and End-User Statement where applicable. No mandatory conversion ratio exists, and no timeline applies for repatriation because the jurisdiction is a dollarized, non-surrender, non-exchange-control territory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banistmo, S.A. (Banco Latinoamericano de Comercio Exterior, S.A. / Bladex group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate feasibility. Panama's banking law restricts the taking of deposits from the public to entities licensed by the Superintendency of Banks; therefore, an offshore digital EMI or electronic money institution without a Panamanian banking or finance-company license cannot operate a deposit-taking account. A PIF may use a licensed Panamanian fintech or a specialized payment processor with a License B or License C general license only as a payment gateway, not as the primary liquidity depository. Cross-border EMIs regulated in the EEA or UK are generally unsuitable as the main account for U.S. dollar clearing of aviation escrow flows because of U.S. correspondent banking restrictions, Travel Rule thresholds, and the requirement for the underlying transaction to be clearly trade-related. The recommended viable structure is a Panamanian bank or trust-company escrow account for contractual aviation deposits, complemented by a U.S. dollar clearing account at a U.S. correspondent bank in the name of the Panamanian bank; direct use of an offshore EMI is advised only for non-core, pre-reconciliation administrative payments and must be avoided for regulated aviation escrow receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is generally required for the initial corporate account opening at most Panamanian banks, particularly for private interest foundations and medium-risk aviation trading entities. The foundation's registered agent (agente residente), the beneficiary, and at least one director or authorized signatory are expected to appear before the bank's compliance officer for an in-person interview and biometric or notarial verification. Remote opening may be available at certain private banks (e.g., Towerbank International and selected trust-oriented banks) if the entity has an existing relationship, the client has been pre-vetted by a licensed Panamanian attorney, and the Identification and Due Diligence File (Expediente Único de Identificación) is completed with notarized and apostilled documents; however, the standard compliance posture for a PIF engaged in aviation parts distribution will require at least one physical visit to Panama for the initial onboarding and for any subsequent change in signatories or beneficial ownership. Electronic signature and videoconference interviews may be accepted as a supplement but not as a complete substitute unless the bank has an express remote-account-opening policy approved by the Superintendency of Banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) used as the direct account holder for a high-value aviation spares trading operation, with opaque or layered beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certificate of the foundation (copia de la escritura pública), registered bylaws, certificate of registered agent, list of council members and beneficiaries, apostilled and notarized; a formal Foundation Council resolution designating authorized signatories and establishing the commercial purpose of aviation spare parts distribution; a complete organizational chart with identification documents of grantor, council members, beneficiaries, and any protector; an economic substance statement explaining the operational nexus in Panama or the foreign-source nature of the income; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for the initial capital contribution; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for using a PIF rather than a Panamanian corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-dollar trade flows to and from jurisdictions with actual or perceived elevated sanctions or AML risk, including transshipment via free-trade-zone airports or brokers in multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous commercial invoices and purchase orders matching the aviation part serial numbers; executed sale or consignment agreements; aviation compliance certifications (FAA Form 8130-3, EASA Form 1, or equivalent export airworthiness certificates); full chain-of-custody documentation for each rotable; certificate of final customer or end-user statement; bill of lading and airway bill with detailed commodity description; and screening results showing no sanctioned parties in the transaction chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of U.S. dollar transactions through an aviation parts trading account with no clear payroll, supplier, or operational expense trail, potentially indicating invoice discounting, cash-pass-through, or trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month projected cash-flow budget prepared by a licensed Panamanian accountant; accounting system reports mapping each inbound wire to a specific purchase order or consignment sale; supplier contracts for surplus airframe disassembly and part refurbishment; aircraft-part inventory ledger with beginning stock, acquisitions, sales, and scrap; payroll and overhead records for any employees or contractors; and contemporary banking correspondence explaining any large or unusual transaction prior to execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of funds from third-party aviation escrow agents or from brokers who are not disclosed on the customs export declaration, creating an inconsistency between invoice payer and actual funding source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement between the PIF, the broker, and the escrow agent; escrow instructions identifying the PIF as the sole beneficiary of the deposit; a reconciliation letter from the escrow agent stating the source of funds for each release; a declaration of non-involvement of third parties in the underlying aviation transaction; and a notarized declaration of the beneficial owner explaining the role of each intermediary, accompanied by relevant licenses or certifications of the intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The recommended compliant routing for initial capital injection and subsequent shareholder/founder funding is a U.S. dollar wire from the grantor or shareholder's verified bank account to the PIF's Panamanian operational account using the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) message type MT103 for straight-through processing. The wire must clearly identify the beneficiary as the PIF with its full registered name and account IBAN or CLABE-style identifier as provided by the Panamanian bank; because Panama does not use IBAN, the bank's ABA/Chapa number and account number must be provided. The payment purpose code should be stated in the remittance field, such as 'GITS' or 'GITM' for transfers to non-resident entities if routed through a U.S. correspondent, or the appropriate ISO 20022/CFS purpose code; a Panamanian bank will generally accept a narrative like 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation [Name] for aviation parts trading' or 'Shareholder loan for working capital – ISIC 4659'. Supporting verification must include a certified capital contribution resolution, a copy of the foundation deed, source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, sale agreement of assets, dividends, or gift letter), and a sworn statement from the grantor that the funds are not derived from proceeds of crime. For transfers exceeding certain thresholds, the bank will file a Currency Transaction Report with the UAF and may inquire into the economic substance of the foundation; thus the injection should be completed in a single transparent wire rather than structured into fragmented deposits to avoid structuring red flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade disbursements is a SWIFT MT103 wire from the Panamanian bank account to the supplier, refurbisher, logistics provider, or escrow agent. For larger aviation-consignment settlements, a commercial letter of credit (LC) issued under UCP 600 rules is appropriate, particularly when the counterparty is a non-U.S. airframe teardown facility or MRO provider; the recommended form is an irrevocable, confirmed (if possible) documentary credit with presentation of the commercial invoice, airway bill, certificate of airworthiness, and packing list. A standby LC or bank guarantee may be required when onboarding new consignment principals. To ensure liquidity clearing in the U.S. dollar system, the funding bank should maintain a nostro relationship with a U.S. clearing bank; payments settle through the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) or Fedwire, and correspondent banks will verify OFAC, anti-boycott, and sanctions screening. For high-value or non-standard disbursements to a third-party payee, the PIF must instruct the bank with a board-authorised payment instruction, and the bank will apply enhanced due diligence where the recipient is located in a higher-risk jurisdiction. The less preferred but viable rail is a commercial draft or cash-in-advance cross-border payment through a specialized aviation escrow provider that holds funds in a fiduciary account at a U.S. bank; such providers may require the PIF to be a named beneficiary and will generally impose a 0.5%–1.5% transaction fee for escrow, wire, and compliance handling.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: U.S. dollar-balboa spot transactions (automatic, no hedging required because the balboa is pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and circulates only as coins)

Cross-currency profit hedging using deliverable forward contracts (plain vanilla forwards) between the U.S. dollar and the customer's settlement currency, e.g., EUR/USD or MXN/USD, provided the Panamanian bank or an affiliated broker-dealer acts as counterparty and the transaction is classified as a trade-related hedge, not a speculative instrument

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American emerging-market currencies such as the Colombian peso, Peruvian sol, or Argentine peso, available through a U.S. or regional bank with a Panamanian booking center, permitted only where the PIF can demonstrate a firm underlying aviation purchase or sale commitment in that currency

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) and rolling spot contracts for managing temporary settlement mismatches between the receipt of U.S. dollars and the need to pay a foreign-currency MRO or teardown facility, subject to the bank's mark-to-market collateral requirements

OTC vanilla currency options (call or put) used as insurance against adverse exchange-rate movements on large bespoke aircraft-rotable purchases, although such options are not customarily offered to a PIF absent a structured relationship with the bank's global markets desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual / Impuesto Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; collection executed through Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge; chronic non-payment for consecutive years places the foundation in inactive status and triggers administrative strike-off from the Registro Público de Panamá, requiring settlement of arrears plus reinstatement filing fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (electronic filing platform under Decreto de Gabinete 233 de 2022, amended by Ley 254 de 2023)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days following the foundation's registry anniversary date; must also be updated within 15 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including transfers of PIF beneficial units
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 5,000 per Ley 254 de 2023; prolonged non-disclosure can result in cancellation of juridical personality and referral to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for AML enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Private Interest Foundation engaged solely in asset holding is exempt from statutory audit; however, a mandatory independent audit by a licensed Panamanian CPA is triggered if the foundation's commercial activity generates annual gross revenue exceeding USD 3,000,000, or if audited financial statements are required by DGI, a financing counterparty, or an aviation supplier certification scheme (EASA/FAA parts distribution verification).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian Local GAAP (Normas de Contabilidad Generalmente Aceptadas de Panamá) for general purposes; full IFRS adoption is required when financial statements are submitted to DGI for cross-border aviation financing or where the surplus aircraft parts trading volume mandates IFRS 15 revenue recognition and IFRS 16 lease scrutiny.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must file the annual sworn UBO declaration through the DGI Beneficiarios Finales portal within 30 days of the registry anniversary, and must furnish an updated confirmation within 15 days of any transfer of beneficial units; the resident agent is legally obligated to retain certified copies of the declaration and the underlying unit-holding ledger for a minimum of 5 years after each change, with an internal retention extension to 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries (Registro de Beneficiarios) with unit-holding schedules
Foundation Council Minute Book (Libro de Actas del Consejo de Fundación)
Accounting Books (Libro de Inventarios y Balances; Libro Diario y Mayor)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% for fiscal year 2025 (25% prior to Law 361 of 2023; scheduled 20% from fiscal year 2026)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxable; foreign-source trading margins on off-shore aircraft parts sales are outside the Panamanian ISR net. Reduced rates apply to SEM (multinational headquarters) licensees (5% local-source ancillary income; 0% on qualifying export services); Zonas Francas users enjoy an effective 0%–5% ISR on qualifying operations. A Private Interest Foundation (Law 25 of 1995) holding non-commercial assets is exempt, but the active distribution of aircraft parts is commercial activity taxable as a corporate trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 700 (Declaración de Renta / Personas Jurídicas) filed via the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax platform ('Sire' / DGI web portal); TP annexure (Form 700 Annex / 'Anexo de Precios de Transferencia') where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: To be filed within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a calendar-year taxpayer by 31 March following the close of the year); payment due with the return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer's Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) number, business name (PIF foundation name), domicile and fiscal year for the declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned PIF must present its RUC and the annual declaration through its resident legal representative; non-residents without a Panama e-Tax password must authorize the representative

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian operations (local sales of aircraft parts, commissions, local services) taxable under the territorial system
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama-source receipts are declared; proceeds from foreign buyers where title/risk passes outside Panama and no Panama PE exists should be excluded and supported by contracts and customs/airway documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Memorandum line showing foreign-source gross revenue used for the proportional taxable-income attribution calculation for mixed activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable portion of local production/administration costs is allocated based on the ratio of Panama-source gross revenue to total gross revenue; foreign-source revenue supports the exclusion

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: allowable deductions / costs of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: COGS, freight, insurance, warehouses, professional fees and operating deductions allocable to Panama-source income; depreciation and amortization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses attributable to foreign-source income are non-deductible against Panama income; invoices must be in order and subject to withholding if paid to non-residents; keep the Partida/ledger (libros) entries consistent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: net taxable income & ISR computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed at 22% (2025) or 20% (2026) after applying NOL carryforwards and any exempt-income exclusions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the 4% 'presunción mínima' catch-up: if calculated taxable income is below 4% of taxable gross revenue, the assessment base is raised to 4% of gross revenue; verify the minimum-tax line

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: dividend tax / capital reduction treatment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the final dividend tax (Law 361 of 2023) on retained profits treated as deemed distributions and the annual prepayment (anticipo) of the dividend tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders of the PIF (founders/beneficiaries) do not file personally; the entity withholds and remits the dividend tax on any distribution or deemed distribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of related-party transactions, method applied (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split), and comparability adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the annexure even where the parent or principal is non-resident; intercompany margins on aircraft spares distribution must be benchmarked to independent distributors

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of gross revenue with the 7% ITBMS (Panama VAT) returns for local sales; exports and qualifying international sales at 0%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the export documentation (bill of lading, airway bill, export declarations) to support zero-rating of outbound aircraft parts; mismatches between ITBMS returns and ISR revenue are a primary audit trigger

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fines of B/.50 to B/.500; late payment: monthly recargo of up to 1% plus statutory interest (approximately 10% per annum); omission of income in the return: penalty of 50%–100% of the tax evaded; non-filing after a DGI notice triggers 'determinación de oficio' (official assessment) and ineligibility for the 'paz y salvo' (clearance) certificate needed for the municipal license and bank transactions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid from profits subject to corporate income tax (increased from 5% by Law 361 of 2023); 15% on dividends/distributions made from profits not previously subject to corporate income tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief: (1) confirm coverage under a Panama DTA (e.g., Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, France, UK, Italy, Portugal, Qatar, UAE, Singapore, South Korea, Mexico, Barbados); (2) obtain the Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority covering the distribution date; (3) legalize/apostille the TRC and provide a Form of declaration of beneficial ownership and the foundation council resolution authorizing the distribution; (4) file the relief application with the withholding agent/local paying foundation before the withholding deadline and, where the rate was applied incorrectly, apply to the DGI for refund within the relevant statute of limitations (generally 5 years); (5) substantiate the beneficial owner, substance abroad, and absence of treaty shopping (PPT/LOB limitation present in modern Panama treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP used in Panama: 12.5% statutory WHT (Panama-source), reducible to 5%–10% under applicable DTAs; technical service fees for aviation engineering/IT used in Panama: 15% statutory WHT (reducible under DTAs); interest paid to non-resident financial or commercial lenders: no statutory Panama WHT (territorial; 0%), provided the lender has no Panama permanent establishment and the loan is bona fide (arm's-length, documented, commercially substantive)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and TP study mandatory where related-party transactions in a fiscal year exceed B/.2,000,000 (US$2,000,000; B/. is pegged 1:1 to USD); Master File required where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent equals or exceeds B/.50,000,000; an abridged TP annexure is filed with Form 700 in all related-party transaction cases
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply (Law 107 of 2020 / implementing decrees) to entities carrying on geography-mobile 'relevant activities', including distribution of goods, financing, leasing and headquarters functions. A PIF trading in aircraft parts must demonstrate: (i) staff with suitable qualifications resident and physically present in Panama, (ii) physical premises and equipment, (iii) core income-generating activities (contract negotiation, inventory management, invoicing and risk control) performed in Panama, and (iv) annual economic substance return filed with the DGI; failure to meet substance exposes the entity to fines, reassessment, and treaty-benefit denial under the OECD/G20 principal-purpose test

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through misdeclared Panama-source income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of local sales of aircraft parts, use of fictitious export documents to convert taxed local income into untaxed foreign-source income, invoice suppression, or false COGS inflation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50%–100% of the evaded tax plus interest; administrative fine of B/.500–B/.5,000 per infraction; the 'Renta presunta' minimum tax (4% of gross) prevents underassessment; criminal liability pursued where the evasion exceeds statutory thresholds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the Foundation Council and officers who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the ISR, surcharges and fines; criminal conviction for tax fraud exposes them to imprisonment (up to 5 years), confiscation of assets, and travel bans/alerts in money-laundering-linked tax cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Private Interest Foundation / acting as a de facto trading corporation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a PIF (Law 25 of 1995) as an operating company for the regular commercial purchase/resale of aircraft parts while claiming foundation exemption, or carrying on business for the sole benefit of the founder with no council governance or accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI and courts may disregard the foundation (veil piercing) and assess corporate ISR, dividend tax, ITBMS and penalties as if the business were a mercantile company; the foundation's assets may be attached for the unpaid fiscal liabilities; revocation of the foundation's registered status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Council members are personally liable for distributions made in insolvency or from untaxed profits; the founder/beneficiaries may be treated as de facto shareholders and taxed on deemed distributions; striking off and 'neutralization' of the entity triggers personal liability for subsequent debts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing and economic substance failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unpriced or mispriced intercompany purchases of surplus inventory from a related foreign supplier, paying excessive commissions to a related procurement agent, or retaining all management functions in a tax haven while booking sales in Panama
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to the arm's-length result; penalty of 40%–50% on the tax understatement arising from TP adjustments; denial of treaty benefits; fines under the ESR (up to B/.1,000,000 in aggravated cases) and possible deregistration of the commercial license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize non-arm's-length invoices without economic substance face personal 'responsabilidad solidaria' for the CNP/DGI claim; in cross-border cases, foreign tax authorities may invoke the DTA exchange-of-information clause, exposing the officers to parallel prosecutions and extradition where trade mispricing is linked to money laundering

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML: trade-based money laundering and sanctions circumvention
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Over/under-invoicing the surplus aircraft parts to move value between jurisdictions, using the PIF to hold the proceeds, receiving Swift wires from non-licensee third parties, dealing with counterparties in OFAC/EU/UN-sanctioned states, or cash-layering of escrow settlements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 (as amended): administrative fines of up to B/.1,000,000 per violation on the entity and responsible compliance officers; freezing/seizure of the aviation inventory and funds; criminal money-laundering conviction carries 5–12 years' imprisonment and asset forfeiture
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, signatories and beneficial owners face personal criminal prosecution, preventive custody and travel bans; bank-account freezes (escrow and Swift rails) are imposed by UAF orders during investigation; professional enablers (abogados, contadores) may also be indicted for facilitating the scheme
